target_customer: Software engineering teams (for example AppFolio, HealthSherpa) that need to keep open source dependencies current
problem: Upgrading open source packages means reading changelogs, judging breaking-change risk and ordering upgrades, which is toilsome work that teams postpone.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus a managed white-glove upgrade service by expert developers
product_category: Developer tools, dependency management and upgrade planning

founders.name: Steve Pike
founders.background_notes: Press release says he consulted on dependency upgrades before founding and was CTO of SevenFifty. Education not found.

founders.name: Allison Pike
education: University of Pennsylvania, BA Political Science and Psychology

founders.name: Andrew Lenehan
founders.background_notes: Named a founder and second-time founder in the January 2024 press release; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Dependabot
competitors.what: Automated pull requests that bump dependencies and fix vulnerable ones
competitors.traction_then: Acquired by GitHub in May 2019 and made free
competitors.funding_then: acquired by GitHub (price not stated in cited source)

competitors.name: Renovate
competitors.what: Configurable dependency update bot that also works on GitLab and Bitbucket

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs per-ecosystem parsing of changelogs and lockfiles and an optimization of upgrade order, plus a database of undocumented incompatibilities; standard engineering with hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: The incompatibility database could compound, but free GitHub-native Dependabot and open source Renovate cover the basic job.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GitHub folded Dependabot into the platform for free in 2019. Infield positions itself above it by planning upgrades and fixing breaking changes.

market_need_then: Dependency drift and supply chain risk were widely felt, and GitHub buying Dependabot in 2019 showed demand for automated upgrades.

branding.domain_note: Uses infield.ai; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical; runs a newsletter called Once a Maintainer.

branding.community_and_virality: Substack newsletter Once a Maintainer; no evidence of wider community buzz.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found only unrelated Infield brands, so the name is shared with others; no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Infield remains active and raised a 3 million dollar seed in January 2024, years after its Winter 2020 batch, which suggests slow, capital efficient building and a late launch of its SaaS platform. It competes with free Dependabot and Renovate and differentiates on upgrade planning and managed service. No acquisition or shutdown was found.
notes: AlleyWatch (2023-03) reported a 2.9M figure from an SEC filing, seen in one snippet only and not recorded as a round. Funding between 2020 and 2023 not found. Renovate source is a secondary discussion, no funding data.
